title: Searching Zscaler logs in Splunk: field names, placeholders and validation searches
aliases: splunk field names for zscaler logs

prose.text: A search can only filter on the names a record carries once it is indexed, and those come from how the feed was written and parsed. Index and source type names are tenant plumbing and are not held here.
An NSS feed replaces each field specifier with its value, in the order written: [[shared.nss.feeds:format-specifiers]], [[shared.nss.feeds:field-order]]. {{name-value-pairs}} {{search-names}}

NSS and LSS field names are case-sensitive: [[zia.logs.nss-feed-format:case-sensitive]], [[zpa.log-receivers.formats:field-names-newline]]. The default LSS templates and their keys are in the log types, for example [[zpa/user-activity-log]]; custom content changes them: [[zpa.log-receivers.formats:custom-content]].

What the Zscaler add-on for Splunk renames is open {{gap:add-on-mapping}}. Source type names per log type are open in [[shared.siem-mapping:splunk-landing]]; a vendor example shows two of them: [[shared.siem-mapping:splunk-example]].

checks.do: Confirm the field names the tenant's feed actually carries (the feed's output format or the receiver's log stream content, and any add-on aliases) before running a search written with NSS or LSS names.
If a search's result depends on an open field question, keep the search and say which question it depends on.

name-value-pairs.statement: Both the NSS feed guidelines and the LSS log stream content guidelines suggest name-value pairs where the SIEM supports them, and say some SIEMs, such as Splunk, can parse name-value formats and auto-detect field names regardless of order.

quotes: Consider using name-value pairs, if your SIEM can support it. Some SIEMs, such as Splunk, can automatically parse name-value formats and auto-detect field names, regardless of the order.

search-names.statement: The names a SIEM search can use therefore come from the feed format and its parsing, not from the specifiers themselves: a positional feed carries only values, and a name such as url exists in the index only if the format writes it as a name-value pair or the SIEM's parsing assigns it, so a search written with NSS or LSS field names works only where the feed or its parsing uses those names.
search-names.conditions: Follows from the feed-format guidance; how a given add-on or parser names positional values is not in any registered source.

add-on-mapping.title: What the Zscaler add-on for Splunk renames
add-on-mapping.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Zscaler Internet Security for Splunk add-on (Splunkbase app 3865) provides field aliases from NSS names to Splunk CIM names (login to user, url to url, host to dest_host, action to action, rulelabel to rule, threatname to threat_name, ssldecrypted to ssl_decrypted, ZPA Username to user, ZPA Application to app) and dashboards; its aliases vary by add-on version, and whether ssl_decrypt or ssldecrypted is the searchable name depends on the version. The legacy table also mapped clientip, sourceip, destip and a firewall proto, which are not names in the ZIA field tables (the web feed has cip, the firewall feed csip, cdip and ipproto). Source type names are a separate question (shared.siem-mapping:splunk-landing). No registered source covers the add-on's aliases.
add-on-mapping.blocks: Writing searches that use CIM names or add-on source types
